newsitem.title: UK: INSIGHT - British Biotech to head for 300p.
newsitem.headline: INSIGHT - British Biotech to head for 300p.

text.p: DAY'S RANGE * SUPPORT * RESTNCE* MA-25 * MA-200
+ A chart break at 240p by British Biotech shares recently implies they can forge ahead to 300p in coming months, technical analyst said.

+ The share price has completed a bullish flag and implied an initial resting place for the stock at 250p. Turnover in the shares has improved as the stock has made its upward push so that its upside potential remains, they added.
Shares in pharmaceuticals group British Biotech have broken above 240p resistance, signalling a move up to 300p, technical analysts said.
"The shares have been rising on high volume and key resistance at 240p has been broken," said Nick Glydon, technical analyst at Robert Fleming Securities.
The shares may pause for a while near 250p before they can drive on, he added.
By 1030 GMT, British Biotech shares were unchanged at 250p.

The shares took a tumble last summer falling to about 190p from a high of 326 in May. There was solid support for the shares at 190p as they travelled sideways meeting resistance at 240p each time they tried to rally until this month.
In the latest move to overcome the 240p barrier a bullish flag was completed and calculations from it suggest that its influence should end around 250p.
A flag pattern is one in which a share price first spikes up sharply then makes a small downward channel before continuing the original upward move.
The length of the original spike up, when added to the point of breakout from the channel, gives the next immediate target.

Turnover in British Biotech shares has gradually improved with a daily average of around two million shares traded since January 10 when they made a low of 194p compared with an average turnover of 0.67 million over the first six working days of the year.
Higher turnover has been registered as the shares marched up this year and this volume has diminished whenever the shares have floated down.
If this turnover pattern continues it implies an upward trend for the shares over the next few months, analysts said.
